items.title: Charles Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 23, 1997
items.q: He had come out of Fletcher Henderson’s era... But he was like with Fletcher Henderson, and we were playing jazz, bebop, whatever.

ctx.x: When people hear the words Sun Ra, if they know at all who he is, I think most of us probably think of the kind of outlandish trappings that went along with all the things he did, but when you started with him in the mid-50s, what kind of music was he doing then?

Well even with all the outlandish trappings as you say, he still played the same thing. He had come out of Fletcher Henderson’s era and then as time progressed, the more the cosmic called him, the more he dealt with that situation. But he was like with Fletcher Henderson, and we were playing jazz, bebop, whatever. He always had a mythical essence to his music anyway.
